FOUR PRODUCTION FINDINGS, all of them real:

  - `_CursorInternals` -- the protocol `bulk.py` and `modules/db.py` reach the
    cursor through -- declared `in_pipeline` as a settable variable, and
    `Cursor.in_pipeline` is a read-only property. mypy therefore said `Cursor`
    does not satisfy the protocol, which is exactly what the TYPE_CHECKING-only
    `_assert_cursor_satisfies_bulk_host` in cursor.py exists to catch, and the
    two `copy_from` call sites in `modules/db.py` inherited it. Declared as a
    property. One line, three errors, and the assertion function does its job
    again.

  - `CommonServer` had no `run`. Every concrete flavour defines one and
    `_factory.py` calls `server.run(preload, stop)` through the base type, so
    the entry point of the whole serving tier was unchecked. Declared, raising
    NotImplementedError with the flavour name.

  - `PreforkServer._census_written_at` is read in `_publish_census` and assigned
    only in `__init__`, further down the file, so mypy could not determine its
    type at the read. Declared on the class.

  - `_limits.py` said `from odoo.tools import config` and then indexed it.
    Under `follow_imports = silent` that name resolves to the SUBMODULE
    `odoo.tools.config`, not to the config object, so `config[key]` was
    indexing a module. `from odoo.tools.config import config` is unambiguous;
    layer_check, facade_surface_check, libs_facade_check and py_addon_imports
    all still pass.

THE TESTS were the other half, and `test_invariants.py` had one shape repeated
eight times: `ast.parse(textwrap.dedent(inspect.getsource(x))).body[0]` typed as
`ast.stmt`, then read for `.body`, `.test` or `.handlers`. `_def_ast()` says it
once and raises if what it parsed is not a def or a class, which is a better
failure than an AttributeError several lines later. Three casts remain where the
test asserts the node type with `assertIsInstance` and then reads it.

Four `type: ignore` are added and each marks a place the type system cannot
follow the runtime: `AttributeError.loglevel` (an attribute the RPC dispatcher
sets and reads), `type(val)(items)` over an arbitrary sequence subclass, the
two-target clear of `_InotifyInternals`, a name-mangled `_Cursor__pool` in a
test, and two `lambda` method assignments in another. `endpoints.py` already
carried one and it named the wrong code -- `arg-type` where mypy reports
`call-overload` -- so it suppressed nothing.
